title: 誰是受益者？
text:
Cui Bono：為何凱文·沃什只是另一隻偽裝的鴿子



讓我們從古羅馬的一則小故事開始。當一位元老院議員在廣場上被發現遇刺身亡時，偉大的演說家西塞羅會向群眾提問：「Cui bono?」- 這對誰有利？誰是受益者？這個簡單的問題往往比任何調查都更快揭開真相。兩千年後的今天，同一提問依然跟燈塔的光芒一樣，引導我們明白現代貨幣政策的底蘊。利益分配 - 而非新聞發布會上的華麗但空洞的詞藻 - 才真正揭示人類行為的背後真相。
公理 1：Cui bono - 這對誰有利？
這是我在這些文章中將經常運用的第一原則。利益激勵不僅包括物質上的豐厚薪酬和獎金，還包括「感覺良好」和「做正確的事」的心理滿足感。
2026 年 6 月 17 日，凱文·沃什作為新任聯儲局主席舉行了首次記者會。他鄭重宣示致力於恢復物價穩定。最近2026年5月的通膨數據年增率升至4.2%，是三年多高位，主要受地緣政治衝突引發的能源價格暴漲所推動。然而，聯儲局卻決定維持利率不變。
評論家們讚歎道：「沃什不一樣！他是真正的鷹派！」
但我不敢苟同。
讓我們用利益激勵因素來分析吧。川普總統是低利率的愛好者。他公開宣稱：「我愛通膨……那些數字很棒。你知道我真正愛什麼嗎？我愛通膨。」因為鮑威爾不肯積極大幅降息，川普猛烈抨擊前主席鮑威爾行動太慢、是「徹底的失敗者」和不懂變通。他把鮑威爾趕走，正是因為這位前主席不願在中期選舉前用寬鬆貨幣政策刺激經濟。
川普會任命一位真正的抗通膨戰士，甘冒經濟放緩風險而大幅加息的人做聯儲局主席嗎？當然不會。沃什得到這個職位，正是因為他會迎合川普的偏好。他只是表面強硬，但實際上會推行寬鬆貨幣政策。
想真正擊敗通膨，需要提高利率並減少印鈔。就這麼簡單。但沃什卻以能源供應衝擊、AI可帶來的生產力大幅提升，以及「需要更多證據」或更好數據作為藉口，宣布成立多個工作小組來「檢討」聯儲局溝通方式、資產負債表、通膨框架等等典型的官僚拖延戰術，繼續量寛政策。
若沃什大幅推升聯邦基金利率，將會讓美國龐大國債的利息支出爆炸性增長。目前淨利息支付已消耗聯邦收入的約18–22%。利率若再升高，這 - 負擔可能膨脹至收入的25%以上，排擠其他所有支出。在政治和財政上，這無異於自殺。因此，最有可能的政策方向是寬鬆。
沃什或許會小幅加息，以對抗持續走高的通膨，但實質利率幾乎肯定仍會維持負值。更重要的是，一旦出現任何經濟麻煩的跡象- 股市下挫、就業數據下滑，或是來自白宮的政治壓力 - 他就會立刻煞車，毫不猶豫地降息。畢竟，關鍵時刻，利益高於一切。
被視為鷹派沃什的首次亮相（點陣圖亦暗示可能升息），最初確實支撐了美元並壓低股市 - 標普500指數當天下跌超過1%，成為數十年來新主席首次聯邦公開市場委員會會議日表現最差之一。黃金與白銀則在恐慌中被壓低至接近200日移動平均線附近。但如果這種鷹派姿態只是表演，劇本就很清楚了：貨幣將持續貶值、美元長期走弱，以及貴金屬作為可靠避風港會繼續上漲。
投資者應考慮黃金和白銀等硬資產，作為對抗長期貨幣貶值的保護。目前兩種金屬在賣壓後正測試其200日移動平均線，這可能是一個好的買入機會。

title: Cui Bono?
text:
Cui Bono: Why Kevin Warsh Is Just Another Dove in Disguise



Let us begin with a little tale from ancient Rome. When a senator was found murdered in the Forum, the great orator Cicero would ask the crowd: Cui bono? — To whom is it a benefit? Who gains? This simple question often unraveled the truth faster than any forensic sleuthing. Fast-forward a couple of millennia, and the same axiom shines like a beacon in the fog of mysterious monetary policy. Incentives, not press-conference mere rhetoric, reveal the truth about human behavior.
Axiom 1: Cui bono — to whom is it a benefit?
This is the first principle I’ll wield frequently in these postings. Incentives include not just material rewards like fat paychecks and bonuses, but also the psychological satisfaction of “feeling good” and “doing the right thing”.
On June 17, 2026, Kevin Warsh held his first press conference as the new Fed Chairman. He professed a solemn commitment to restoring price stability. Recent inflation? A stubborn 4.2% year-over-year in May 2026 — the highest in over three years, driven largely by surging energy prices amid geopolitical fireworks. Yet the Fed left interest rates unchanged.
Pundits swooned: “Warsh is different! A real hawk!”
I beg to differ.
Let’s follow the incentives, shall we? President Trump is a low-interest-rate guy. He openly declared, “I love the inflation… The numbers were great. You know what I really love? I love the inflation.” Trump hammered prior Chair Jerome Powell as “Mr. Too Late,” a “major loser,” and a “real stiff” for not slashing rates aggressively enough. He pushed Powell aside precisely because the old chair wouldn’t goose the economy with easy money ahead of the midterms.
Would Trump appoint a genuine inflation warrior who’d hike rates and risk a slowdown? Of course not. Warsh got the job because the incentives align. He will talk tough but deliver accommodation. Pretend hawkishness is the perfect cover.
Truly slaying inflation requires higher rates and less money printing. Simple as that. Instead, Warsh offered excuses centered on supply shocks (energy, etc.), productivity hopes (thanks to AI), and the need for “more evidence” or better data. He announced task forces to “review” communications, the balance sheet, inflation frameworks, and more — classic bureaucratic delay tactics while the printing press stays warm.
Pushing the fed funds rate meaningfully higher would explode interest costs on the US gargantuan national debt, not to mention risking Trump’s mid-term election. Net interest payments already consume roughly 18–22% of federal revenues. At higher rates, that burden could balloon toward 25%+ of revenue, crowding out everything else. Politically and financially suicidal it is. So incentives says the most likely way forward is continued accommodation and money printing.
Warsh may raise rates modestly to fight inflation if the latter continues to go higher, but real interest rates would almost certainly remain negative. More importantly, the moment there’s even the slightest hint of economic trouble — a wobble in the stock market, a dip in employment, or political pressure from the White House — he will slam on the brakes and cut rates without hesitation. After all, when push comes to shove, the incentives always win.
Warsh’s perceived hawkish debut (with the dot plot hinting at possible hikes) initially strengthened the dollar and pressured stocks — the S&P 500 dropped over 1% that day, marking one of the worst first-Fed-day performances in decades. Gold and silver were slammed toward their 200-day moving averages amid the scare. But if this hawkishness is mostly theater (as incentives strongly suggest), the long-term script is clear: persistent currency debasement, a weaker U.S. Dollar over time, and higher precious metals as the reliable escape hatch.
Investors would do well to consider hard assets like gold and silver as protection against long-term currency debasement. With both metals recently testing their 200-day moving averages after the selloff, this could turn out to be a compelling buying opportunity.

title: My First Post
text:
This is my first post!
‘If you wish to be a writer, write.’ … Epictetus
I always want to write about logical and critical thinking based on some self-evident axioms, and use these axioms to analyse human behaviour in general, and economics and financial investments in particular, and hopefully the approach would lead me to make sound investment decisions. I have procrastinated for a long time until very recently, I came across the above Epictetus quote, and finally decided to give it a go.
I would hope that I can start a community of like-minded people to subscribe to my blog, and obtain feedback for mutual improvement and satisfaction.
My plan is to post one or two pieces each week.

title: 谁是受益者？
text:
Cui Bono：为何凯文·沃什只是另一只伪装的鸽子



让我们从古罗马的一则小故事开始。当一位元老院议员在广场上被发现遇刺身亡时，伟大的演说家西塞罗会向群众提问：「Cui bono?」- 这对谁有利？谁是受益者？这个简单的问题往往比任何调查都更快揭开真相。两千年后的今天，同一提问依然跟灯塔的光芒一样，引导我们明白现代货币政策的底蕴。利益分配 - 而非新闻发布会上的华丽但空洞的词藻 - 才真正揭示人类行为的背后真相。
公理 1：Cui bono - 这对谁有利？ 
这是我在这些文章中将经常运用的第一原则。利益激励不仅包括物质上的丰厚薪酬和奖金，还包括「感觉良好」和「做正确的事」的心理满足感。
2026 年 6 月 17 日，凯文·沃什作为新任联储局主席举行了首次记者会。他郑重宣示致力于恢复物价稳定。最近2026年5月的通膨数据年增率升至4.2%，是三年多高位，主要受地缘政治冲突引发的能源价格暴涨所推动。然而，联储局却决定维持利率不变。
评论家们赞叹道：「沃什不一样！他是真正的鹰派！」
但我不敢苟同。
让我们利用益激励因素来分析吧。川普总统是低利率的爱好者。他公开宣称：「我爱通膨……那些数字很棒。你知道我真正爱什么吗？我爱通膨。」因为鲍威尔不肯积极大幅降息，川普猛烈抨击前主席鲍威尔行动太慢、是「彻底的失败者」和不懂变通。他把鲍威尔赶走，正是因为这位前主席不愿在中期选举前用宽松货币政策刺激经济。
川普会任命一位真正的抗通膨战士，甘冒经济放缓风险而大幅加息的人做联储局主席吗？当然不会。沃什得到这个职位，正是因为他会迎合川普的偏好。他只是表面强硬，但实际上会推行宽松货币政策。
想真正击败通膨，需要提高利率并减少印钞。就这么简单。但沃什却以能源供应冲击、AI可带来的生产力大幅提升，以及「需要更多证据」或更好数据作为借口，宣布成立多个工作小组来「检讨」联储局沟通方式、资产负债表、通膨框架等等典型的官僚拖延战术，继续量寛政策。
若沃什大幅推升联邦基金利率，将会让美国庞大国债的利息支出爆炸性增长。目前净利息支付已消耗联邦收入的约18–22%。利率若再升高，这一负担可能膨胀至收入的25%以上，排挤其他所有支出。在政治和财政上，这无异于自杀。因此，最有可能的政策方向是宽松。
沃什或许会小幅加息，以对抗持续走高的通膨，但实质利率几乎肯定仍会维持负值。更重要的是，一旦出现任何经济麻烦的迹象- 股市下挫、就业数据下滑，或是来自白宫的政治压力 - 他就会立刻煞车，毫不犹豫地降息。毕竟，关键时刻，利益高于一切。
被视为鹰派沃什的首次亮相（点阵图亦暗示可能升息），最初确实支撑了美元并压低股市 - 标普500指数当天下跌超过1%，成为数十年来新主席首次联邦公开市场委员会会议日表现最差之一。黄金与白银则在恐慌中被压低至接近200日移动平均线附近。但如果这种鹰派姿态只是表演，剧本就很清楚了：货币将持续贬值、美元长期走弱，以及贵金属作为可靠避风港会继续上涨。
投资者应考虑黄金和白银等硬资产，作为对抗长期货币贬值的保护。目前两种金属在卖压后正测试其200日移动平均线，这可能是一个好的买入机会。
